newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian military protest against cutbacks.
newsitem.headline: Belgian military protest against cutbacks.

text.p: Some 4,000 Belgian military, or nearly one in 10 of the country's armed forces, marched through the streets of the capital on Sunday throwing firecrackers to protest against further job cuts.

"There's money for the EU but not for the Belgian people," said one banner, as marchers clad in blue, green and red plastic union capes vented their anger in the shadow of the European Parliament's new multi-million-dollar headquarters.

The military were complaining about inadequate compensation for those leaving the services and the threat of further cutbacks if the military budget is not raised after the current restructuring programme ends in 1999.
The Belgian chief of staff, Vice Admiral Willy Herteleer, has given a warning that a 10-billion-franc ($300 million) increase is needed to avert a further 8,000 job losses.
Around one in five military are already being demobilised under a programme started in 1993 as the country adjusted to the post-Cold War era and budget austerity.
"We don't want to be menaced with more cutbacks. We want adequate financial aid for those leaving," Freddie Libin, one of the march leaders, told Reuters.

Sunday's march was the latest in a series of mass protests in Belgium which have seen civil servants and private-sector steel workers demonstrating against spending cuts as the country struggles to qualify to join a single EU currency in 1999.
